key_insight: Quantum virtual-phonon coupling reshapes the predicted shift-current spectrum of monolayer MoS2 even at zero temperature, despite barely changing its band dispersion.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for electron–phonon coupling could improve nonlinear photocurrent predictions and guide strain- and temperature-based tuning of optoelectronic devices.
method: Include zero-point electron–phonon renormalization of electronic states.
Evaluate shift-current responses to strain and temperature.
evidence_signal: Calculations predict new low-energy peaks, redshifted higher-energy features, strong tuning under 1.0% strain, and enhanced band-renormalized shift current with increasing temperature.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational results for one material, not experimental validation, solar-cell efficiency gains, or AI-based optimization.
paper_title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
